evidence.claim: Cattle roads and power projects became a journey through the high Sierra.
evidence.quote: Its principal routes, Beasore Road and Minarets Road, originated as access roads for ranching and hydroelectric development.

evidence.claim: The Sierra Vista Scenic Byway links high meadows, granite domes and the San Joaquin River canyon in the Sierra National Forest.
evidence.quote: The route passes the San Joaquin River canyon, Mammoth Pool Reservoir, high-elevation meadows and granite domes

evidence.claim: The Forest Service describes a 100-mile drive taking about five hours, highlighting Sierra Nevada scenery and views.
evidence.quote: meanders for 100 miles through the Forest highlighting some of the most beautiful scenery and views of the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range. The Scenic Byway takes about 5 hours to drive

evidence.claim: Designated a National Forest Scenic Byway in July 1989, it joined a program created to give access to scenic, recreational and historic features.
evidence.quote: The Forest Service established its National Forest Scenic Byways Program in May 1988 to identify existing roads providing access to scenic, recreational, and historic features. The Sierra Vista route was designated a National Forest Scenic Byway in July 1989.

evidence.claim: The byway designation also aimed to support nearby rural economies. Local residents formed the Sierra Vista Scenic Byway Association in 1990 to promote and develop the route.
evidence.quote: Economic development in nearby rural communities, particularly North Fork, was among the goals of the designation. In April 1990, local residents formed the Sierra Vista Scenic Byway Association to promote and develop the route.
